name: France
summary: Strict prohibition: any use of a stupéfiant is a crime (up to 1 year and €3,750). Police often use a €200 fixed criminal fine (AFD) for cannabis, cocaine or ecstasy. Harm reduction incl. drug checking is legal.

poisonControl.name: Centre antipoison de Paris (regional centres nationwide)

callingForHelp: SAMU (15) doctors are bound by medical secrecy, but police may also attend. No Good Samaritan law; failing to help a person in danger is itself an offence.
drugChecking: Allowed within the harm-reduction framework (2016 health law); offered by some CAARUD and associations, varies by city.

disUsage.title: Drogues Info Service: drug use and the law (AFD amounts, alternatives)

disInterdites.title: Drogues Info Service: prohibited drugs (ANSM stupéfiants list)

csp.title: Public Health Code (Code de la santé publique), Légifrance

anN2O.title: Assemblée nationale: bill restricting nitrous oxide sales to professionals (adopted 29 Jan 2025)

srfN2O.title: SRF: France plans to criminalise nitrous oxide use (May 2026)

lsd.note: Stupéfiant. Use is a crime (up to 1 year, €3,750); possession and supply are punished far more heavily.

mushrooms.note: Psilocybin and hallucinogenic mushrooms (Psilocybe, Stropharia, Conocybe…) are stupéfiants; truffles included.

dmt.note: Stupéfiant. Ayahuasca and its source plants are also classified as stupéfiants (since 2005).

mescaline.note: Mescaline is a stupéfiant. Mescaline cacti are sold as ornamentals; their status when intended for consumption was not verified.

dox.note: DOM, DOB and DOC are internationally controlled and classified as stupéfiants.

nbomes.note: 25B-, 25C- and 25I-NBOMe are internationally controlled stupéfiants; other analogues may also be listed.

5-meo-xxt.note: Not internationally controlled. We could not verify whether 5-MeO-DMT or 5-MeO-MiPT are on France's stupéfiants list.

cannabis.note: Use is a crime; police often issue a €200 fixed criminal fine (AFD), recorded on the criminal record. Low-THC CBD (≤0.3%) is legal.

ketamine.note: Stupéfiant used in anaesthesia (and as esketamine spray). Possession without prescription is treated like other illegal drugs.

dxm.note: Prescription-only since July 2017 because of recreational misuse; not a stupéfiant.

nitrous.note: Adults may possess it. Supply to minors and sales in bars/tobacconists banned (2021); many local bans. Stricter bills pending.

amphetamines.note: Amphetamine and methamphetamine are stupéfiants. Methylphenidate for ADHD is available only on secure prescription.

mdma.note: Stupéfiant. Use is a crime, often handled with the €200 AFD; possession and supply much heavier.

cocaine.note: Stupéfiant. Use is a crime, often handled with the €200 AFD (recorded); trafficking up to 10 years or more.

caffeine.note: Not a controlled substance; sold freely.

alcohol.note: Legal for adults; selling or giving alcohol to under-18s is banned.

ghb/gbl.note: GHB is a stupéfiant (sodium oxybate on prescription). GBL and 1,4-BD are not stupéfiants, but selling them to the public is banned.

opioids.note: Heroin is banned; morphine, oxycodone and fentanyl are stupéfiants on secure prescription only.

tramadol.note: Prescription-only; since 2025 it must be prescribed on a secure prescription (ordonnance sécurisée).

benzodiazepines.note: Prescription-only psychotropic medicines; some need a secure prescription. Possession without prescription is an offence.

maois.note: Harmala alkaloids, Syrian rue and Banisteriopsis caapi are stupéfiants (2005), so ayahuasca is illegal. Moclobemide etc. on prescription.
